Joint Committee on Transportation Public Hearing, Month, Day, 2025
Written Testimony in Support of Bill 164, An Act to Exempt Authorized Emergency Vehicles from Tolls When Operating in an Official Capacity

Senator Nangle, Representative Crafts and members of the Joint Committee on
Transportation.

My name is Dale Rowley, and I live in Winterport. I am the Director of the Waldo County Emergency Management Agency. I am here today to testify in support of the bill. I am
also offering suggestions to improve it.

Although Waldo County does not contain a section of the Maine Turnpike, I have responded to emergencies where I have needed to use the Maine Turnpike. All sixteen county emergency management agencies maintain a shared mutual aid agreement with one another and have assisted one another during emergency events. I personally have responded to York County to help staff their Emergency Operations Center during the Mother's Day Floods of 2006. Recently, Penobscot County Emergency Management deployed with an emergency management vehicle and staff to the flooding in North
Carolina.

I do believe that emergency response vehicles should be exempt from paying the Turnpike Tolls when responding to an emergency. Taxpayer funds from a county or municipality should not have to be utilized to pay the tolls during a response.
What I would like to see changed with the bill, is to add emergency management to the list of "Authorized Emergency Vehicles" under Title 29-A, section 2054, subsection 1,
paragraph B.

Emergency management agencies operate mobile command posts, emergency
communications vehicles and trailers, disaster logistics vehicles, and staff response vehicles. If the Emergency Management program is under a fire department or law enforcement department, its vehicles are considered authorized emergency vehicles.
However, if the exact same vehicles performing the exact same emergency response mission are operated by a standalone emergency management department, such as a County Emergency Management Agency, they are not considered thus.

Testimony of Erin Courtney, Maine Turnpike Authority Before the 182'" Legislature, Joint Standing Committee on Transportation

Neither for Nor Against LD 164 "An Act to Exempt Authorized Emergency Vehicles from
Tolls When Operating in an Official Capacity"

Senator Nangle, Representative Crafts, and distinguished members of the Joint Standing
Committee on Transportation, l am Erin Courtney, Director of Communications and Government Relations for the l\/laine Turnpike Authority (MTA). MTA is neither for nor against LD 164, "An Act to Exempt Authorized Emergency Vehicles from Tolls When Operating in an Official Capacity."
We support the concept of assisting local emergency responders. The MTA currently funds 100
percent of the operations of Troop G of the l\/laine State Police-an annual investment of over $7
million. These officers are dedicated solely to patrolling the l\/laine Turnpike. Additionally, emergency vehicles responding to incidents on the Turnpike are already exempt from tolls.
We respect and value the essential work performed by emergency personnel, and we appreciate
the sponsor's intent behind this bill. However, as currently drafted, we have serious concerns
that prevent us from supporting LD 164 in its current form.

The definition of "authorized emergency vehicles" includes 28 separate categories of vehicles operated by a wide range of state, federal, municipal, and even university agencies. This includes not only ambulances, fire trucks, and police cruisers--but also correctional transport vehicles, railroad police, federal law enforcement vehicles, and others.

First, the l\/lTA`s tolling system is not currently designed to automatically identify or differentiate all these various types of vehicles, especially those that are not clearly marked as emergency vehicles. There is no single data source or tag identifier that universally captures this entire
category of vehicles. As such, determining the scope of toll usage across all of these entities would require writing special code that would allow us to run a query for this information. This is a labor intensive task that would require more time in order for us to know what the impact to toll revenue would be.
Second, becauseghe MTA is a toll-funded entity with no state funding, any loss in toll revenue will have implicatj ns for our operations, maintenance, and capital improvement projects. We
don't know what that amount would be right now and we would need some time to determine

Senator Nangle, Representative Crafts and Esteemed Members of the Joint Standing
Committee on Transportation, I am Mathew Mclntyre and I humbly serve as the
Representative for Maine's House District 18 comprising 16 towns and four Unorganized Territories spanning portions of Penobscot, Hancock and Washington counties. Today I
offer testimony as the sponsor of LD164, "An Act to Exempt Authorized Emergency
Vehicles from Tolls When Operating in an Official Capacity" .
As I begin, I offer my presentation today as a direct result of engaging fire and EMS
entities throughout District 18, and I serve proudly in carrying their voices here for your
respectful consideration.
Per Maine Revised Statutes Title 23, Part l, Subsection 1973, Paragraph 3 "Tolls, or the fixing of tolls, is not rulemaking and is not subject to supervision or regulation by any state commission, board or agency" . Additionally, within Subsection 1973, Paragraph 5 establishes an exemption for "Use by military" . I pose these facts as an example of the foundation for what I believe can certainly be categorized as comrnon-sense legislation,
and I ask that you join me in supporting this Act.
While fire and EMS providers throughout Maine are facing multiple challenges in terms
of recruiting, retention, increasing training requirements and regulatory compliance, today's discussion shall be focused solely on addressing just one aspect; rapidly increasing operational budgets. This proposal, while seemingly minor in the grand
scheme, represents one small step in the right direction.
As just one example, the Central Maine Highlands Fire and EMS District #1 provides
essential services to eight Towns and portions of Unorganized Territories in both Penobscot and Hancock counties. Their small but loyal team of first responders protects the lives and property of over 4,000 regional souls for most of the year, with that number seeing significant jumps during peak "camping" season. They do all of this on what is an
incredibly tight budget, and far too often Department Command is forced to make
difficult decisions as where to make cuts, just to keep the doors open and the community protected. This one department annually budgets approximately $1500 to cover expenses incurred through Maine Turnpike tolls, and I pose this to be utterly umiecessary, and inappropriate. While $1500 may not seem like a lot, I assure you that Department
Command would prefer to use it in more effective manners that directly benefit the
community they serve, such as equipment, supplies or training. $1500 equates to three pair of fire boots, or 3 fire helmets, or one Automated External Defibrillator (AED), or a
video laryngoscope. I personally would consider these much more useful investments
into the inventory of any department.
House District 18

Through bipartisan support of this cormnon-sense legislation, we have an opportunity to
reduce one small measure of budgetary struggle for the heroes that keep us safe. Additionally, in eliminating just a single unnecessary expense for our first responder
departments, we will in turn help to reduce local property taxes. I for one would call this
win-win, and I trust that you must clearly see it the same way. I thank you for your time today, and look forward to continuing this discussion during future work sessions. It is imperative I mention that since I first drafted this testimony I have engaged several helpful and transparent conversations with key stakeholders, so if the legislation initially drafted by the Revisor's Office requires reasonable amendments, I
am willing to participate in the work needed to get this effort to "Yes" . I will be glad to address any questions you may now have.
